issues.legal_issue: A person for whose benefit land is acquired and who bears the compensation is a person interested in the acquisition proceedings and may be joined as a proper party.
material_facts: Land was acquired for the appellant company’s benefit, and the company would bear the compensation payable for it.
The lower courts refused to treat the beneficiary as a person interested or to implead it in the compensation proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiary was a person interested under section 3(b) and a proper party under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the contrary orders were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, contains an inclusive definition that is to be construed liberally. A beneficiary that bears the compensation has a direct interest in both the compensation and the land acquired for its benefit. The Court followed Himalayan Tiles & Marbles (P) Ltd. v. Francis Victor Coutinho, Neelagangabai v. State of Karnataka, Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti v. Ashok Singhal, Union of India v. District Judge, Udhampur, Union of India v. Sher Singh, Bihar State Electricity Board v. State of Bihar, Union of India v. Kolluni Ramaiah, and N. Krishnamachari v. Managing Director, APSRTC. It held Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad v. Chandulal Shamaldas Patel to be no longer good law and distinguished Santosh Kumar v. Central Warehousing Corporation.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land and determination of compensation for it.
predicates.land_acquired_for_beneficiary: The land was acquired for the benefit of a person or entity other than the acquiring authority.
predicates.beneficiary_bears_compensation: The beneficiary is responsible for bearing the compensation payable for the acquired land.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for a beneficiary that bears the compensation, the beneficiary is an interested party in the acquisition proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary that bears the compensation may participate in compensation proceedings, present and test evidence, and be heard; the statutory right to adduce evidence does not exhaust its procedural rights.
material_facts: The beneficiary sought to participate in pending references to determine compensation, including by adducing evidence.
The lower courts rejected its applications on the ground that it was not a person interested.
The beneficiary would bear any increased compensation, and the government’s participation might not adequately contest claims for an increase.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiary was entitled to be impleaded in the pending references, to cross-examine the claimants’ witnesses, to adduce rebuttal evidence, and to be heard on just and proper compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(b) and 50(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, must be read together. Section 50(2), which permits a company or local authority to adduce evidence before the Collector or the court, is additional to—not a substitute for—the procedural rights that follow from being a person interested. Those rights include a fair opportunity to be heard, consistent with Article 14 of the Constitution. Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure supports joining the beneficiary as a proper, if not necessary, party. The Court relied on the line of authority beginning with Himalayan Tiles and including Neelagangabai, Krishi Upaj Mandi Samiti, Union of India v. Sher Singh, and the other beneficiary cases it reviewed.

predicates.compensation_determination_proceeding: The proceeding determines compensation for acquired land, including a proceeding before the Collector or a court reference.
predicates.land_acquired_for_beneficiary: The land was acquired for the benefit of a person or entity other than the acquiring authority.
predicates.beneficiary_bears_compensation: The beneficiary is responsible for bearing the compensation payable for the acquired land.

issues.definition: In a compensation-determination proceeding, a beneficiary that bears the compensation may participate, test and present evidence, and contest the amount.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary that was not heard and is adversely affected by a compensation award may challenge it through an appropriate appeal or writ proceeding.
material_facts: The beneficiary had not been joined in the proceedings in which compensation was determined or enhanced.
The beneficiary sought to challenge the resulting awards, including by writ petitions and by seeking to participate in appeals.
The beneficiary would bear the financial burden of the enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiary was entitled to challenge an adverse compensation determination, including by seeking leave to appeal or by a writ petition where appropriate. The dismissed writ petitions were directed to be treated as appeals under section 54 and disposed of with the State’s pending appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(b), 18, 26, 50(2), and 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, read with Article 226 of the Constitution and Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, permit a beneficiary that is a person interested to challenge an adverse award when it was not heard. It may seek leave to appeal against an enhanced award, defend the Collector’s award, or invoke writ jurisdiction to challenge an award made without notice; an award of the Collector may also be challenged where vitiated by fraud, collusion, or corruption. The Court relied on Neelagangabai, N. Krishnamachari, and the other beneficiary authorities, and explained that Santosh Kumar concerned a different issue about seeking a reference from the Collector’s award.

rule.if: challenge_to_compensation_award and land_acquired_for_beneficiary and beneficiary_bears_compensation and beneficiary_not_heard

predicates.challenge_to_compensation_award: The proceeding seeks review of an award determining compensation for acquired land.
predicates.land_acquired_for_beneficiary: The land was acquired for the benefit of a person or entity other than the acquiring authority.
predicates.beneficiary_bears_compensation: The beneficiary is responsible for bearing the compensation payable for the acquired land.
predicates.beneficiary_not_heard: The beneficiary was not given an opportunity to participate and be heard before the compensation award was made.

issues.definition: A beneficiary that bears the compensation may challenge an adverse award when it was not heard before the award was made.
